data.one_liner: Retrieve information about screen size, displays, and cursor position for Flutter desktop apps
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter desktop applications to read display information including size, work area, and scale factor. It also tracks cursor positions and listens to display change events like additions and removals.
use_when: You are building a Flutter desktop application for macOS, Windows, or Linux.
Your application needs to get information about multi-monitor setups, screen resolution, or work area bounds.
You need to listen for display connection changes at runtime.
avoid_when: You are building a mobile or web-only application.
You only need general device information unrelated to screens.
strengths: Supports multiple desktop platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux).
Provides live reading of display properties and native display IDs.
Includes event handling for display add, remove, and change events.
weaknesses: Requires specific development libraries on Linux build machines (GTK 3, X11, Xi).
Older 0.2.x API versions are deprecated and being phased out.
data.setup_notes: Linux build machines need GTK 3, X11 and Xi development files installed via apt.
